transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, they say I’m here because... I used up our savings. I went and bought a whole lot of wood, lights, and display stuff, and I just kept pushing the work, you know, way after dark. 

But the thing is, I felt like if I stopped doing it, the whole house and the rest of the block would just... lose its chance. I really believed I had to keep going.
When you felt you had to keep working to save the block, did you hear any voices or see anything that others around you could not see?

No, I didn't hear anyone talking to me, and I didn't see anything out of the ordinary. It wasn't like that. It was just... well, it was just this really strong feeling I had inside. I just knew I had to get it done, or else. But no, no voices or anything like that.
When you felt that the house and the block would lose their chance if you stopped working, did you believe that you had some sort of special power or a unique mission that other people didn't have?

Well, I don't know about special powers or anything like that. But a unique mission... yeah, I suppose you could call it that. 

I know people think I’m just mixed up in the head right now. But I am sure this neighborhood was picked for my last big civic art piece. I was the one supposed to put it together. And I know I'm right about it because of the signs. Just little things, you know? Like the delivery trucks slowing way down when they drive past the house, or the neighbors always looking over from their yards. That proves they know it too. They know something important is happening.
During the time you were working on this project, how many hours of sleep were you getting each night, and did you feel tired the next day?

Well, I'm not really sure how many hours it was. I wasn't looking at the clock or keeping track of the time when I was out there. I just worked. 

And as for feeling tired... I don't really remember feeling tired the next day. I just knew I had to keep going, so I didn't really notice it if I was.
During those days when you were working constantly, did you feel unusually energized, or perhaps more talkative or excited than you usually are?

Yeah, I did. Most days I just felt... well, really charged up. Almost joyful, to be honest with you. It felt like I was young again, having all that energy to just go out there and get things done. 

But... I guess I also had a pretty short fuse. If my wife came out and started questioning me, or if the contractors asked what I was doing, I'd get hot fast. I'd just start yelling at them to leave me alone and let me work. So yeah, I was energized, but you definitely didn't want to get in my way.
Have you ever had other periods in your life, besides this one, where you felt this same intense energy, had big plans, and felt like you were on a special mission?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times in my life where I worked hard on things, sure, but... nothing quite like this. I've never felt this kind of pull before, like I had to do something this important. This was the first time I felt like I had a real mission to finish.
Since this period of intense energy ended, have you felt unusually sad, hopeless, or lost interest in the things you typically enjoy?

No, I can't say that I have. I mean, I haven't been feeling sad or down in the dumps or anything. I just... well, I don't have that same fire I had when I was working out there. Things are just back to being quiet. But no, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless.
About how long did this period of feeling charged up and working on your project last before things started to quiet down?
Well, I'd say it went on for about three months. It all started when the remodeling began and everything in the house got turned upside down. That's when I really got going on it.

Now that you aren't working on the project with that same fire, do you still believe that the neighborhood was specifically chosen for your civic art piece and that the trucks and neighbors are signaling to you that something important is happening?

Well, no, not really anymore. I mean, before I got so charged up with the remodeling plans, I wasn’t seeing any special meaning in the trucks driving by or the looks my neighbors were giving me. I didn't think twice about them. All those signs... they really only started once I felt so driven to turn the house into that big civic project. Now that the fire is gone and things are quiet, they just seem like regular trucks again.
